LESSON: WEATHER AND CLIMATE

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 1.4: Weather and Climate

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Weather and Climate. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we experience different climatic conditions in Kenya?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify elements of weather in the environment
2. show main climatic regions in Kenya on a map
3. describe characteristics of the main climatic regions in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WEATHER AND CLIMATE
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Weather and Climate helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: WEATHER AND CLIMATE
Weather and Climate is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Identify elements of weather in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to identify elements of weather in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify elements of weather in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Weather and Climate” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify elements of weather in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Show main climatic regions in Kenya on a map

What this means
In this part you learn to show main climatic regions in Kenya on a map. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show main climatic regions in Kenya on a map.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Weather and Climate matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show main climatic regions in Kenya on a map. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe characteristics of the main climatic regions in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to describe characteristics of the main climatic regions in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe characteristics of the main climatic regions in Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Weather and Climate this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe characteristics of the main climatic regions in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Weather and Climate is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Weather and Climate” around your school. (skill: identify elements of weather in the environment)

Example 2: Say why Weather and Climate matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: show main climatic regions in Kenya on a map)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Weather and Climate this week. (skill: describe characteristics of the main climatic regions in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Weather and Climate to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify elements of weather in the environment.
3. Practise this skill: show main climatic regions in Kenya on a map.
4. Practise this skill: describe characteristics of the main climatic regions in Kenya.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Weather and Climate from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Weather and Climate: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Weather and Climate?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we experience different climatic conditions in Kenya?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Weather and Climate means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify elements of weather in the environment.
5. Be able to: show main climatic regions in Kenya on a map.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
